visualCharacteristics.purpose: Page-opening image with a headline and call to action
visualCharacteristics.layout: Background image fills the block; content row sits on top
visualCharacteristics.home: Full-bleed photo with a centered H2 headline and a CTA button below it
visualCharacteristics.centered: Centered column: eyebrow then H1 (max ≈680px), text max-width 760px, centered; vertical padding ≈ 96px top/bottom on desktop. Eyebrow: mono font, 11px, uppercase, letter-spacing 0.18em, muted color. H1: display font, 700, ≈2.7rem desktop / 1.8rem mobile, line-height 1.08, letter-spacing -0.03em. Body: 18px / 1.7, secondary text color. Primary button: pill (radius full), accent background, white text, 16px 600, padding 15px 30px, glow shadow, trailing arrow →. Secondary button: pill, translucent surface background with a 1px strong border, primary text color.

contentPattern.structure: row 1: background image; row 2: heading (H1 or H2) and an optional CTA link in its own paragraph
contentPattern.example: Background image, H2 'A great place to do meaningful work.', CTA 'Find Your Next Role'
contentPattern.centered: Same two-row hero model (image row optional/empty, content row). Content: first paragraph before the H1 is the eyebrow; H1; body paragraphs; bold link = primary button, italic link = secondary button.
contentPattern.centeredExample: Empty image row; content: eyebrow 'Careers', H1 'Help us fix healthcare.', two paragraphs, bold link View All Open Positions, italic link Submit Your Resume

reuseGuidance: Use plain 'Hero' for the boilerplate left-aligned hero; add the 'home' option for the full-bleed centered homepage hero. A lone link in the content row becomes a button under 'home'. For interior page headers (H1 and intro beside a photo with a curved corner) use 'Columns (curve)'. Add the 'centered' option for a text-only intro: optional eyebrow paragraph before the H1, body copy and CTA buttons (bold link = primary, italic link = secondary) centered side by side; the image row may be left empty.
notes: The former 'page' variation (page header) is now the Columns (curve) block.
